explanation: Fantasia's Fantasound system sent music around the cinema from separate speakers in 1940, though only a handful of cinemas installed it. Stereo LP records reached the shops in 1958.

claims.text: Disney's Fantasia was shown with its stereophonic Fantasound system in 1940.
Stereo LP records first went on sale to the public in 1958.
Only a handful of cinemas were fitted with Fantasound.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic02w. Claims: every checkable statement in the labels, values and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers sound technology, so both dates need web evidence from the checkers. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for 'b': stereo feels like a home-hi-fi invention of the 1950s, which is the trap. Argued against the key: Fantasia's Fantasound premiere was in November 1940 and commercial stereo LPs arrived in 1958, 18 years later. Neither label claims a first, so earlier stereo experiments do not affect the answer. Counterintuitive is true, so both label claims are high under C26. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: Fantasia and stereo records are known worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: None.

evidence.restatement: Stereo LP records went on sale in 1958, although Audio Fidelity issued the first commercial stereo LPs in late 1957 (and Cook's binaural discs sold earlier in the 1950s), so 'first went on sale in 1958' may not be what every source says.

claimResults.note: No web search was possible (budget exhausted). The key survives any of these dates because Fantasia is 17 or more years earlier, but the date as written is a first-on-sale claim with conflicting sources. Needs external evidence.

evidence.restatement: Only a small number of cinemas (roughly a dozen or fewer) were fitted with Fantasound.

claimResults.note: 'A handful' is loose if the count was about a dozen; it is accurate in spirit.

issues.note: c2 and the explanation state that stereo LPs reached shops in 1958. Sources differ (late 1957 for the first commercial stereo LPs; 1958 for the major labels' releases). Step down the precision ladder: 'stereo LPs reached shops by 1958' or 'in the late 1950s', and keep the label and values consistent.

editor.reason: A pass, B revise. B's issue on c2 is real: both checkers independently cite stereo discs on sale before 1958 (Cook's two-groove binaural records from 1952, Audio Fidelity's stereo disc in late 1957), so label b 'Stereo records go on sale' shown as 1958 is open to a pedant even though the key holds under every reading. The fix (a tighter label and a year every source agrees on) changes label b, the values and c2, so it is not a wording-only rewrite, and a tiebreak could only confirm the imprecision (§9.7). c1 to c3 are also high risk on knowledge only. Cut. Redraft under a new id, for example 'Single-groove stereo LPs go on sale', with web evidence.
